meaning: to share the same understanding of a situation, so that people can work together without confusion
literal_translation: aynı şeyi anlamak ve aynı fikirde olmak
example: Before the meeting, the two delegations confirmed that they were on the same page about the agenda.
origin: Probably from the practice of reading the same printed document during a meeting; the exact origin is uncertain

wrong_meanings.meaning: to read the same book at the same time as a friend
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This takes the words literally, but the idiom describes shared understanding in a discussion, not reading the same text

wrong_meanings.meaning: to share a single page of a notebook
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom has nothing to do with notebooks or sharing paper

wrong_meanings.meaning: to turn the pages of a document quickly
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom describes agreement about meaning, not the physical movement of pages

explanation: 'Be on the same page' means that everyone involved understands a situation in the same way, which makes cooperation easier. It is common in diplomatic and business negotiations.
